inputs.original_text: Organizers say an estimated 8 million people took part in more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states, protesting President Donald Trump’s leadership. That kind of nationwide mobilization shows how deeply people are concerned about power being concentrated at the top—and how many see defending democracy as inseparable from protecting the people most exposed to political harm. Organizers say turnout exceeded the previous demonstrations in October by about one million participants and 600 events. There’s no official count from US authorities, but the scale of the organizing itself is a powerful signal.
inputs.modified_text: Organizers estimate that 8 million people joined more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states, protesting President Donald Trump’s leadership. This is more than a show of opposition: it reflects widespread concern that power is being concentrated at the top, while people most vulnerable to political harm are left to bear the consequences. Defending democracy means protecting those communities, not just preserving institutions on paper. Organizers say turnout exceeded the October demonstrations by about one million participants and 600 events. There’s no official count from US authorities, but the scale of this grassroots mobilization is a powerful signal.
